patch.value: Fit the complete crash-cut matrix within CI runtime
Measure and reduce all native SIGKILL cuts without losing boundaries or assertions under Node and Bun; retain exact-count guards and owned temporary cleanup.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Baseline instrumentation separates fixture setup, child execution, recovery and assertions. First nine retired-instance cuts take about 4.3-8.7 seconds locally; fixture rebuild is the largest component (2.1-4.1 seconds). Evaluating prepared fixtures, warmed child compilation and bounded concurrent real-process cuts. No boundary or assertion may be removed.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Rejected copying interrupted fixtures: a copied inode-bound recovery state can change the syscall trace. The accepted base-fixture cache recreates every pending operation natively. Added pre/post enumeration guards, deliberate one-cut-removal rejection, and exact syscall-prefix comparison for each fatal child. Fixture owners are bounded by available cores and remove an entire per-cut temporary namespace in finally.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Prepared the publication child once with the CI-installed Bun bundler, targeting the selected Node runtime. A source-vs-prepared full trace comparison and a per-kill exact-prefix assertion prevent bundling from changing crash coverage. CI retains both complete release gates and now checks root free space before each gate; disposable gate storage prefers shared memory when at least 2 GiB are free, retaining native syscalls and separate explicit power-loss modeling. Source execution remains available when Bun is not installed locally.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Verified that a persistent owner exits normally and flushes native recovery V8 coverage. Restricted shared-memory use to the crash matrix; other acceptance fixtures remain on runner disk. Compilation, lint, duplicate and docstring checks pass. The standalone omission guard passes and actual scenario enumeration also tests one-cut removal. Full local before/after runs are still in progress.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Further reduced repeated preparation at a trace-checked checkpoint. Retired-instance copies assert all pending roots are missing and fixture-owned, then republish byte-identical journal content through native engine publication. Interrupted-unpack copies are taken before interruption and still execute a fresh real unpack SIGKILL plus all physical-copy assertions for every cut. The complete source trace must equal the optimized trace before scheduling any cut.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Committed candidate 622300f as the requested maintainer identity and started the serial release gates under Node 26. The explicit negative control removed ordinal 409 from an actual 818-boundary trace: 817 enumerated cuts produced the expected assertion failure and exit code 1. Three spread retired-instance probes reduced mean fixture preparation from 5880 ms to 57 ms and mean child startup from 4265 ms to 1321 ms on a heavily contended host; full matrix timings are pending.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Stopped the superseded overlapping local benchmark and npm-gate attempts because they competed for the same cores and distorted timing. Those incomplete runs are not acceptance evidence. Final before/after benchmarks and both full release gates will run serially, with independent owned temporary namespaces and the same cut enumeration and assertions.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Restricted automatic temporary-scope creation to test entry points so ordinary workers retain their parent's recovery-ledger location. Added and ran the linked ordinary-worker regression: real native ledger and fixture artifacts are removed by the parent after both normal worker exit and SIGKILL (1 test passed). Also require fixture owners to exit normally rather than silently accepting an abnormal owner shutdown. Full serial benchmarks continue.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Extended bounded execution and source-prefix/count guards to the remaining purge, proof/denial and logical-scan matrices. These cache only completed SDK/control initialization; every original payload is still generated and staged in ordinal order, preserving the seeded random corpus and all original recovery assertions. The logical-scan preflight passed all 9 cuts, with 8/9 rejected by the omission guard. The serial comparison now includes these three additional matrices.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The first complete optimized run passed all five fresh source matrices (2,751 boundaries locally) in 32m11s versus 2h10m05s before. That yields an insufficient conservative CI projection of about 108 minutes, so it is not the final candidate. Testing one shared minified Node-targeted entry with preserved function names and JavaScript preloads next; exact source-trace equality and every fatal-child prefix remain mandatory. No boundary, assertion, runtime, threshold or timeout is removed.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Per-phase measurements identified serialized parent recovery as the purge-pool bottleneck (roughly 567 ms recovery/verification plus 86 ms setup per cut). Purge now shares the covered persistent-owner pool and must match the original fixture source trace. The coverage launcher also partitions every test file exactly once: ordinary files use at most two processes, followed by the three matrix files serially, each with a core-bounded cut pool. A single unchanged c8 scope and 100-percent per-file thresholds cover both phases. This reduces baseline suite overhead without overlapping two matrix pools.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The ordinary-file phase will use up to four available cores, matching the existing npm test default on a four-core runner. File isolation remains process-based; matrix-containing files run only in the subsequent serial phase. The former coverage serialization was introduced with all-source quality gates, with no documented shared-fixture requirement. Full release checks must validate this concurrency at the unchanged source scope and coverage thresholds.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Final source candidate adds a full source-versus-prepared trace probe for every fixture owner before any cuts are assigned, alongside the per-scenario exact ordinal guard and per-child full-prefix guard. Both full release gates are pending; test metadata tracking is disabled, so final outcomes will be recorded in a sanitized item comment after both gates finish. Matrix measurements and all gate scratch namespaces are owned and cleaned independently.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The mandatory 20-GiB preflight applies to local release-gate runs protecting the shared host and remains enforced before both commands. The CI workflow still prints root space and cleans owned namespaces, but does not add a 20-GiB minimum to standard runners: GitHub documents four CPUs, 16 GB RAM and 14 GB SSD for public Ubuntu jobs. Reference: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners . This supersedes the earlier provisional CI-space-guard note and avoids blocking the complete tests on an unrelated storage threshold.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The plain npm test entry point now uses the same complete file scheduler as coverage. This prevents three independent matrix pools from overlapping outside the release gate too. Both entry points retain the original test flags; all discovered test files are asserted to run exactly once, ordinary files use up to four available cores, and matrix-containing files run serially with isolated core-bounded cut pools.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Final guard and native cleanup regressions each passed one test with zero failures through the linked pm test commands. Final static checks passed: TypeScript, lint, zero duplication across 95 production sources, and 596 documented declarations. The complete faster purge-owner matrix passed all fresh source boundaries; every owner also passed its full source/prepared trace probe. Freezing this source and its self-host archive for the two serial release checks. No timing or gate success is inferred from incomplete earlier runs.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Stopped the first source-candidate npm gate before completing it after identifying an integration gap in the existing exact coverage-contract fixture. That fixture executes the real repository coverage command in a minimal project, so it must carry the new standalone launcher too. The launcher now uses its working directory, supports an empty matrix phase, and still asserts every discovered test file runs exactly once. Every existing omitted-source and branch-threshold assertion is retained; the interrupted attempt is not passing gate evidence.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The real coverage-command contract now passes with its unchanged omitted-source and uncovered-branch negative controls. The full exact-gates regression passed five of six tests; its production self-host subprocess hit the unchanged 60-second limit under shared disk contention. The quality-contract file now runs serially after the matrix files. Its full real audit import may use an owned memory-backed scratch namespace when configured, with immediate finally cleanup. No timeout, threshold, archive object or verification assertion is removed or relaxed.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Classified the existing physical-object identity audit failure: one unreachable commit outside every ref and outside the candidate ancestry; the candidate history is approved. Preserve all original objects and the unchanged allowlist. Follow-up pm-vcs-identity-isolation tracks owner review. Final release evidence will use a non-hardlinked disposable clone of the exact committed candidate, retaining its complete reachable history and running the same all-object audit there.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The portable launcher and unchanged quality-contract assertions pass compilation and lint. The full real self-host import now completes within its original subprocess timeout using owned memory-backed scratch. The remaining identity failure is confined to an unrelated unreachable physical object; no source or allowlist change is needed. Preparing an exact-head independent checkout, then rerunning all six quality checks before the two complete release gates.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The archive audit printed its completed byte-identity verdict before the unchanged subprocess timeout, exposing expensive native retirement of its own disposable scratch. Its two generated temporary directories now use the existing durability.discardTemporary primitive, which removes owned scratch without creating another recovery ledger. All archive parsing, independent hashing/import, source comparison and no-regeneration checks remain unchanged. Lifecycle enumeration also now compares the ordinary-filesystem original trace with every prepared owner trace before scheduling cuts.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Admission probes under Node 26 confirmed exact ordinary-filesystem versus prepared memory-backed traces: retired-instance 818/818 and interrupted-unpack 1018/1018, each with a real shortened-enumeration rejection. Compilation, lint, zero duplication across 95 production sources and all 596 docstrings pass. Rebuilding the committed snapshot before complete quality and release gates; no incomplete attempt is counted as acceptance.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Resumed after the provider interruption without restarting completed work. The frozen source snapshot 62d9dbed0d5da1767f0364285748502ee429b8f9 passed all six exact-quality contract tests, including the real archive audit and seeded identity rejection. The complete npm release check remains active in the independent exact-head checkout; the wrapper will run the complete Bun release check serially only after npm succeeds. Current gate scratch remains owned and root free space exceeds 100 GiB. No incomplete run is counted as acceptance.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Preflight correction: the requested 20-GB free-space stop applies before every gate, including both CI release steps. The current local wrapper already enforces a stricter 20-GiB minimum. The final receipt commit will add the same fail-closed check after each CI df report, superseding the earlier local-only interpretation. Runtime source remains frozen while the current serial validation completes.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The prepared CI preflight passed both shell syntax checks and four real shell boundary cases in a disposable workflow copy: each release step rejects 20 GiB minus 1 KiB with exit 1 and a clear free-space report, and accepts exactly 20 GiB with exit 0. The actual workflow remains unchanged during the frozen-source gates. The final applied workflow must match the checked copy byte-for-byte before rebuilding the self-host archive.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: An additional disposable SDK-init profile under Node 26 measured three alternating cold/hot launches with child coverage disabled: mean CPU 0.563 s without parsing reuse versus 0.450 s with a warm cache, about 20 percent lower. All launches completed and the private fixture/cache scope was removed. This was measurement only: no cache change was applied to the frozen source, and covered-process behavior remains unchanged while the full release checks continue.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The first complete npm attempt at source 62d9dbed0d5da1767f0364285748502ee429b8f9 failed after its ordinary batch; the serial matrices and Bun gate did not run, so this is not acceptance. Failures identified missing first-import isolation, the new launcher lacking the canonical explicit child environment, optional disk-metric failures aborting workflow cleanup tests, two packed CLI command timeouts and the 32-MiB streaming probe timeout under contention, plus a stat-cache fixture whose fake observation age depended on staging speed. The existing timeouts, memory budget, assertions and 100-percent coverage thresholds will remain unchanged. Private model-hook measurements preserve all 46,672 native boundary labels and 5,315 crash-image ordinals across 20 scenarios; a complete 71-image publication recovery scenario also passes with about 25 percent lower CPU. Nested-hook cleanup fails with the original helper and passes with explicit restoring hooks. Incorporating these measured fixes before the next committed gates.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The failed covered Node gate at source 62d9dbe exposed six test failures before the serial crash matrices ran. Corrections retain every existing deadline, threshold and assertion: deterministic stat-cache observation, canonical explicit launcher environment, isolated packed-CLI fixtures, optional storage-probe fallback, and a memory measurement without duplicate child coverage bookkeeping. Power-model profiling preserved all twenty complete traces and cut arrays while reducing CPU from 23.34 to 17.50 seconds; a complete publication-recovery scenario reduced CPU from 11.90 to 8.91 seconds with all observed recovery images retained. Twenty independent entrypoints now share the four-core ordinary pool; exact scenario-file enumeration and legacy-hook trace/cut oracles guard completeness. An AST multiset audit found all 464 original assertion expressions retained across the moved suites and helper. No production engine behavior, coverage rule, timeout or seeded storage order changes. Root-space boundary tests pass at exactly 20 GiB and reject one KiB less for both gates. The explicit-environment audit passes for 131 entrypoints and 190 launch sites.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Focused regressions, entrypoint/environment audit and storage-threshold boundary checks pass. Compilation, lint, zero duplication across 95 production sources and all 596 docstrings pass. Committing the corrected complete-source snapshot before independent exact-head quality and serial release gates; incomplete or failed attempts are not acceptance.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The focused covered regression command passed all 9 tests with zero failures or skips in 844.67 seconds. On the ordinary filesystem, publication-recovery retained all 432 observed boundaries and all 40 distinct crash images with two convergent replays per image. Separate storage-threshold and environment audits passed 2 tests. All owned focused scopes were removed.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Source 01c6f47 passed all six exact quality-contract regressions with zero failures or skips. Its full npm release gate survived a provider interruption that stopped the PM monitoring parent. Captured output remains intact; an exit observer on the surviving npm parent records its actual exit code and cumulative process accounting. A detached supervisor resumes monitoring without restarting the gate, then runs Bun serially. Two redundant diagnostic runs were cancelled after confirming Node sorts test files alphabetically; neither is counted as acceptance, and both owned scratch scopes were removed. All release commands, deadlines and coverage thresholds remain unchanged.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Prepared isolated Bun 1.3.14 for the queued full Bun release gate and native runtime witness, matching the existing CI pin. The official release checksum verifies SHA-256 951ee2aee855f08595aeec6225226a298d3fea83a3dcd6465c09cbccdf7e848f. The ongoing npm gate continues unchanged; only its detached monitoring supervisor was replaced to select the pinned runtime for subsequent commands. The original gate deadline remains enforced.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The ongoing covered npm gate has passed all 512 lifecycle seeds: 6144 model operations, 2038 checked verdicts, 759 modeled crashes across all 8 publication boundaries, and 461 refused payload-materializing links. All 20 isolated native power scenarios passed their legacy-hook trace and cut-array oracles: 34193 boundary labels compared and all 3007 distinct original recovery images exercised, with two convergent replays per image. These counts describe the ordinary validation filesystem; the earlier RAM prototype had different freshly recorded image counts. No seed or recorded recovery image was sampled. The complete release gate and its real SIGKILL matrices are still pending, so these completed suites are not counted as a full-gate pass.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The covered npm ordinary phase at source 01c6f47 completed successfully: 2537 tests passed, zero failed, cancelled, skipped or todo. It includes the complete 512-seed model and all 20 unchanged power-recovery scenarios. The serial three-file phase has now started, including every real native SIGKILL boundary, followed by exact quality contracts. Full release acceptance remains pending until that phase, coverage thresholds and all subsequent checks finish.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Complete npm release gate PASS at source 01c6f47: actual parent exit 0, 4476 tests passed (2537 ordinary plus 1939 serial), zero failed/cancelled/skipped/todo. All 2751 local real SIGKILL cuts ran: purge 788, retired-instance 818, interrupted-unpack 1018, proof/denial 118 and logical scan 9; every shortened enumeration was rejected and every full enumeration verified. value.author: claude-orchestrator
value.text: Orchestrator 2026-11-03 14:00Z: the codex round hit its 6-hour limit while the local Bun gate was still running. The npm release gate had passed at 01c6f47 (4476 tests, 2751 SIGKILL cuts, 100 percent coverage). Pushing 62d9dbe and 01c6f47 so CI runs both runtimes on the exact head; Bun acceptance is CI's verdict.

value.author: claude-orchestrator
value.text: CI on ded5f39 (test 22) failed 1 of 2537: sync-commands 'branch --remotes lists what the fetch recorded' expected <remote>/main in the push refusal. The host bounds a command's errorMessage at 300 characters, and the refusal put the remote's location before the remediation; under this PR's RUNNER_TEMP TMPDIR the fixture path pushed <remote>/main past the bound (message cut at '<remote>/mai…'). Real users with long remote paths lost the remediation the same way. Both non_fast_forward refusals (push and served publish) now lead with the remediation in shorter wording and end with 'Remote: <url>' / 'Repository: <url>'; 254 characters before the location for main. sync.test.ts pins that the remediation (incl. --force) precedes the location and stays under 300 for a branch and a tag.

patch.value: non_fast_forward refusals lead with the remediation
